Most of our money sits where hard bidding does not work

Three choices you may question

1
Supply risk is not supplier riskOur suppliers are healthy. The materials behind them come mostly from one country: China.
2
Switching time beats supplier countA new cell supplier needs 2 to 3 years to qualify.
3
Chips are Bottleneck, not StrategicA chip is cheap, but it can stop a plant.

56% is Strategic or Bottleneck: we need partnership and risk control, not hard bidding.

Bubble area = annual spend (est.). Scores are ours: profit impact = share of spend, price position, quality; supply risk = qualified suppliers, geographic concentration, switching time, regulation. * Rare-earth magnets sit inside e-powertrain.

Decision 1

Dual source 55/45

CATL Debrecen and LG Energy Solution Wrocław

12.5 GWh a year2028 to 2032

Approve ≈ €6 m a year to make the second source real.

CATL
55%
LGES
45%

Assumptions (est.): the second source can add 25% of its yearly allocation within one quarter (capacity-reservation clause); ≈ 5,650 cars a week; ≈ €3,000 contribution per car, so ≈ €17 m a week. 4.5 extra weeks ≈ €75 m.

The scorecard cannot pick one winner, and that is useful

A 0.02 gap is not a decision

4.25CATL4.27LG Energy Solution

The winner changes with the weights

More weight on cost (45%): CATL wins by 0.20.
More weight on ESG (20%): LGES wins by 0.11.

So we have two good suppliers

That is exactly what a dual source needs.

The others

Envision AESC: third bidder and back-up (it makes NCM at Douai). Verkor: candidate for the third source. ACC: out.

Scores 1 (weak) to 5 (strong) are our own assessment from public data. Weights were fixed before scoring; in the tests the other weights are rescaled in proportion. Try the buttons above the table.

RFQ bids, € per kWh our simulation

Open book

Bidders get our 13-line cost model and must correct it, or they are out.

E-auction

English reverse, only on conversion and margin. Material follows an index.

Simulated bids are our assumption, consistent with the cost model (CATL ≈3% below LGES). English reverse auction because bids are close; a Dutch reverse auction fits bids that are far apart.

We open at €88, aim for €100 and walk away at €108

Our BATNA is weak

We cannot just leave: a new supplier needs 2–3 years. Moving the volume to the other suppliers costs €115.7/kWh. We walk away earlier, at €108: above it, paying for a third supplier is better.

Three levers move their floor

More volume, longer term−€3.5
The index formula−€2.5
Prepayment on cathode−€1.0
Floor: €103 → €96−€7

Anchor on the model

€88 = today's €110 minus the full 20% technology gain. We open with our cost model, not only with a number.

If we land at €103
≈ €88 m

price saving a year vs today's €110
reaches the P&L

≈ €159 m

cost avoided a year vs our BATNA
does not reach the P&L

BATNA: ≈ 9 GWh to LGES at ≈ +3% and 3.5 GWh of NCM back to AESC at ≈ +€12/kWh. ZOPA × 12.5 GWh ≈ €246 m a year. Price saving = (old − new price) × volume; cost avoidance = (BATNA − new price) × volume.

One contract, one clause that pays for itself, and three decisions

Five years, 2028–2032 · 12.5 GWh a year · fixed price with economic price adjustment

Material 47%Conversion and overhead 44%9%
IndexedFollows market indices (lithium, aluminium, copper, graphite). Quarterly reset, ±15% collar.
Fixed, −3% a yearFixed in € per kWh, with a yearly cost-down and an open-book review.
Margin in €Fixed in euros, not in percent.
Service level

99.5% on time in full · ≤ 25 PPM · battery health ≥ 70% over 10 years

Penalties

€25,000 per hour of line stop, capped at 8% of yearly value · CO₂ bonus

ESG

Passport data before orders · audit down to sub-tiers · exit after a failed 90-day plan

Resilience

Export controls are not force majeure · 4 weeks of cathode and anode stock

Technology

Cell-to-pack know-how licensed for a second supplier · take-or-pay on 70%

Exit, payment, law

Break right in year 3 · net 60 days · French law, ICC Paris

Three decisions we need from you today

  1. 1
    The 55/45 dual sourceCATL Debrecen and LG Energy Solution Wrocław, ≈ €6 m a year
  2. 2
    The three-layer priceindexed material, fixed conversion, margin in euros
  3. 3
    €45 m for a third supplierqualify a European LFP source for 2029, over three years

Contract type: fixed price with economic price adjustment (FP-EPA) plus incentives. The margin effect (≈ €16.5 m a year, ≈ 1.2% of category spend) is cost avoidance, not a price saving.
